title: Voluntary Income Tax Withholding from Unemployment Benefits
content:
Under Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders, federal income tax withholding (Voluntary Federal Income Tax Withholding) and state income tax withholding (Voluntary State Income Tax Withholding) are voluntary elections. They start, take effect, stop and end on the following conditions.

## Conditions

**1. The claimant's own choice.** Federal and state income tax withholding are voluntary: only the claimant may start or stop them, by the kind's withholding certificate online or on paper, and an agent records the claimant's request rather than deciding it.

**2. Claim status when the election is started.** A voluntary election may be started only while the claim it is made on has status filed, active, on hold or inactive. The status that counts is the status of that claim as shown in the Department's claim record at the time the election is to be recorded; a claim in any other status does not admit a new election.

**3. Effective date.** The election applies to payments issued on or after its effective date, which is the kind's effective lead business days after it is recorded, counted in business days (Monday through Friday excluding state holidays). Nothing is withheld from payments issued earlier, and no catch-up deduction is taken. The election is requested from the day it is recorded and becomes active when it reaches its effective date.

**4. Change limit.** The claimant may start or stop an election no more than the kind's change limit per benefit year of the claim. The count is the number of elections of the same kind started on that claim plus the number of those elections revoked, within the benefit year of the claim the election was made on.

**5. Stopping.** An election is stopped (revoked) when the claimant confirms stopping it, whether before or after it has taken effect. A revocation stops deductions from payments issued after the kind's revocation lead business days.

**6. End with the claim; calendar-year rate.** A voluntary election ends when its claim closes or is withdrawn and does not carry to a later claim. The state rate in force applies from the first payment of each calendar year.

**7. Year-end reporting.** The year's federal and state withholding is reported on the claim's Form 1099-G in the kind's box.

## Claim status at the start of an election

| Status of the claim the election is made on | New voluntary election |
|---|---|
| Filed | May be started |
| Active | May be started |
| On hold | May be started |
| Inactive | May be started |
| Any other status | May not be started |

## Effective-date examples (hypothetical dates and lead)

*For illustration only, the lead is taken here as two business days; the actual lead is the kind's own figure.*

| Election recorded | State holiday in the period | Business days counted | Effective date | Payment issued on the Tuesday | Payment issued on the Wednesday |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | None | Tuesday (1), Wednesday (2) | Wednesday | Nothing withheld; never caught up | Withheld (on the effective date) |

| Election recorded | State holiday in the period | Business days counted | Effective date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thursday | The Friday | Monday (1), Tuesday (2) | Tuesday of the following week |

A payment issued on the effective date is covered, because the election applies on or after that date; a payment issued the day before is not.

## Change-limit example (hypothetical limit)

*For illustration only, the change limit is taken as two.* On one claim and within its benefit year, a claimant starts a federal election (count 1) and later stops it (count 2). A further start of a federal election on that claim in the same benefit year would exceed the limit. A state election on the same claim is counted separately, because the count is per kind.

## Revocation example (hypothetical dates and lead)

*For illustration only, the revocation lead is taken as two business days.* A claimant confirms stopping an active election on a Monday with no state holiday that week; the two business days run Tuesday and Wednesday. A payment issued on the Thursday, after the revocation lead, carries no deduction under that election, and neither does any later payment.
